subject_definition: Covers algebra, geometry, trigonometry, calculus, and probability. Builds logical reasoning, quantitative thinking, and strong problem-solving foundations for academics and technical careers.
industry_relevance: Essential for engineering, analytics, finance, data science, and aptitude-heavy roles.

subject_definition: Explores motion, force, energy, electricity, optics, and modern physics. Helps students understand real-world phenomena through scientific reasoning and mathematical application.
industry_relevance: Useful for engineering, hardware, research, robotics, and analytical problem-solving roles.

subject_definition: Introduces physical, organic, and inorganic chemistry with focus on matter, reactions, bonding, and materials. Builds conceptual clarity for science-based learning and applied industries.
industry_relevance: Relevant for chemical, pharmaceutical, materials, biotech, and process-driven industries.

subject_definition: Develops grammar, vocabulary, reading, writing, and communication clarity. Supports better expression, comprehension, and confidence in academic and professional settings.
industry_relevance: Critical for interviews, teamwork, documentation, client communication, and workplace success.

subject_definition: Builds quantitative ability, logical reasoning, data interpretation, and problem-solving speed. Important for placement preparation, competitive tests, and decision-making tasks.
industry_relevance: Highly relevant for placements, consulting, analytics, operations, and entrance assessments.

subject_definition: Covers variables, control flow, functions, arrays, and problem-solving basics in programming. Forms the entry point to software development and coding interviews.
industry_relevance: Required for software engineering, testing, scripting, automation, and technical interviews.

subject_definition: Teaches classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism, abstraction, and encapsulation. Helps students write modular, reusable, and maintainable software systems.
industry_relevance: Important for software development, backend systems, enterprise apps, and code design.

subject_definition: Focuses on arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, and hashing. Helps organize data efficiently for scalable problem-solving and coding rounds.
industry_relevance: Crucial for software engineering, product development, and technical interview performance.

subject_definition: Covers searching, sorting, recursion, greedy methods, dynamic programming, and graph algorithms. Trains students to solve problems efficiently with optimized logic.
industry_relevance: Core requirement for SDE, competitive coding, research, and systems roles.

subject_definition: Explains relational databases, SQL, normalization, indexing, and transactions. Helps manage structured data used in real-world software systems.
industry_relevance: Important for backend, analytics, product engineering, and database administration roles.

subject_definition: Covers processes, scheduling, memory management, file systems, and concurrency. Helps students understand how software interacts with hardware resources.
industry_relevance: Important for systems engineering, backend development, embedded systems, and interviews.

subject_definition: Teaches network models, routing, transport protocols, and communication principles. Builds understanding of how devices and services exchange data.
industry_relevance: Useful for backend, cloud, DevOps, cybersecurity, and network engineering roles.

subject_definition: Focuses on software lifecycle, requirement analysis, design, testing, maintenance, and teamwork. Helps build reliable software through systematic practices.
industry_relevance: Important for development teams, QA, project execution, and product delivery.

subject_definition: Covers frontend, backend basics, APIs, HTTP, and web architecture. Helps students build modern web applications used across industries.
industry_relevance: Highly relevant for frontend, backend, full stack, startup, and product roles.

subject_definition: Introduces cloud infrastructure, virtualization, deployment, scaling, and managed services. Helps students understand modern application hosting and operations.
industry_relevance: Useful for DevOps, backend, infrastructure, SRE, and platform engineering roles.

subject_definition: Covers security principles, threats, encryption, access control, and secure practices. Helps protect systems, users, and data in digital environments.
industry_relevance: Relevant for security analysis, compliance, secure engineering, and SOC roles.

subject_definition: Focuses on supervised and unsupervised learning, model evaluation, and feature-based prediction. Helps students understand data-driven intelligence systems.
industry_relevance: Essential for data science, ML engineering, AI product development, and analytics.

subject_definition: Covers intelligent agents, search, reasoning, planning, and applied AI methods. Helps students understand how machines simulate decision-making and problem-solving.
industry_relevance: Relevant for AI engineering, automation, robotics, and intelligent product systems.

subject_definition: Explains data cleaning, statistics, interpretation, dashboards, and business insights. Helps students convert raw data into meaningful decisions.
industry_relevance: Important for analyst, BI, product, operations, and data-driven business roles.

subject_definition: Covers CI/CD, automation, containers, monitoring, and deployment workflows. Helps teams build, test, and release software efficiently and reliably.
industry_relevance: Critical for DevOps, SRE, platform engineering, cloud operations, and release management.
